articles.text: LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Jiàoshòu, nín zǎo!
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Good morning, Professor!
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Zǎo, nǐ hǎo! Zǎoshangde kōngqì bǐjiào xīnxian yìdiǎnr. Wǒ hěn xǐhuan zǎoshang zài wàimiàn zǒuyizǒu.
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Good morning, how are you. The morning air is a little fresher. I like to go for a walk outside in the morning.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Jīntian tiānqi yě bú cuò, méiyou fēng, chūlai zǒuzou duì shēntǐ yǒu hǎochu.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: The weather is pretty nice today too. There's no wind. It's good for the health to go out and do some walking.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Shì a! Jīntiānde tiānqi zhēn shūfu.
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Yes. The weather today is really pleasant.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Jiàoshòu, nín jīntian hǎoxiàng hěn gāoxìng ma!
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Professor, you seem so happy today.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Wǒ hěn gāoxìng. Nǐ zhīdao, hǎo jiǔ le, wǒ xiǎng qù kànkan Běidà, kěshi yìzhí méiyou jīhui qù.
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Yes, I am. You know, I've been wanting to go visit Běijīng University for such a long time, but I never had the chance to.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Jīntian wǒmen jiù kěyi qù cānguān le.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: But we're going today.

ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Shì a. Wǒ shi gǎo jiàoyù gōngzuòde. Zài Měiguóde shíhou, wǒ chángcháng xǐhuan kàn xiē guānyú Zhōngguó jiàoyù qíngkuàngde shū, kěshi, yào zhēnde yánjiūde huà, zǒng juéde cáiliào bú gòu, yǒu hěn duō dōngxi bú gòu liǎojiě. Érqiě, yǒu shíhou yǒude cáiliào hé Zhōngguóde qíngkuàng chābié hěn dà, suǒyǐ...

PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: That's right. I'm in education. When I'm in the States I often like to read books about education in China, but I always feel that we don't have enough data to do actual research on it. There's a lot we don't understand well enough. Furthermore, some of the data is very different from the true situation in China, so...
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Nín yǒu shénme wèntí jiù tíchulai, yěxǔ wǒ kěyi bāng nín yìdiǎnr máng ne?
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Ask me any questions you have, maybe I can help you with them.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Nǐ děngyiděng, wǒ shìshi, kàn néng bu néng shuōqīngchu a!
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Wait a second, let me try and see if I can explain it clearly.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Méi guānxi, nín mànmānr shuō.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: It doesn't matter, take your time.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Zài nǐmen zhèr, dàxué fēn yīlèi èrlèi, zhōngxué xiǎoxué yě yǒu zhòngdiǎn zhōng-xiǎoxué hé pǔtōng zhōng-xiǎoxuéde qūbié. Zhèiyang zuòde mùdì shi shénme ne? Wǒ shi shuō...

PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Here, your universities are divided into Class I and Class II, and your middle schools and elementary schools distinguish between key and regular ones. What is the purpose for doing that? I mean...
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Ǹg, nǐ shuōxiaqu.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Uh-huh, go on.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Wǒde yìsi shi, yàoshi bǎ zhòngdiǎn fàng zài jǐge xuéxiàoshang, néng bu néng pǔbiàn tígāo jiàoyù shuǐpíng ne?
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: I mean, if you put the emphasis on a few schools, will you be able to make a general improvement in the level of education?
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Zhèi shi yíge hěn hǎode wèntí. Nǐ zhīdao, Zhōngguó yǒu shíyìduō rénkǒu, yǒu nàme duō rén xūyào shòu jiàoyù, kěshi jiàoyùde qíngkuàng bù néng ràng rén mǎnyì.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: That's a very good question. You know, China has over a billion people. There are so many people who need to get an education, but educational conditions are not satisfactory.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Ǹg.
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Uh-huh.

LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Tèbié shi jīngguò Wénhuà Dà Gémìng yǐhòu, jiàoyù fāngmiàn zhēn yǒu bù shǎo wèntí, suǒyǐ zài mùqiánde qíngkuàng xia, wǒmen děi bǎ zhòngdiǎn fàng zài yíbùfen dàxué, zhōngxué, hé xiǎoxuéshang.

LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Especially since the Cultural Revolution, there have been a lot of problems in the area of education, so under the present conditions, we must put the emphasis on a portion of our colleges, middle schools, and elementary schools.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Nàme, zài zhòngdiǎn dàxuéli, nǐmen rènwéi zuì zhǔyàode gōngzuò yòu shi shénme ne?
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Then in key colleges, what do you consider to be the principal job?
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Shǒuxiān děi xiǎng bànfǎ tígāo jiàoshīde shuǐpíng. Xiànzài jiàoshī shùliàng bú gòu, shuǐpíng bù gāo.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: First of all we must try to raise the level of the instructors. At present the number of instructors is insufficient and their level is low.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Ǹg, zhèi shi yíge zhòngyàode wèntí.
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Mm, that's an important problem.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Shì, zhèige wèntí hé tígāo zhěnggèr mínzúde jiàoyù shuǐpíng yǒu hěn dàde guānxi.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Yes, it's a question that has great bearing on raising the educational level of the whole nation.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Hǎo, nàme dì'èr ne?
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Okay, then the second thing?
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Gǎo Sìge Xiàndàihuà xūyào hěn duō shòuguo jiàoyùde rén, kěshi zhèijiàn shì bú shi zài duǎn shíjiānli kěyi zuòhǎode. Zhèi yìdiǎn nín dàgài tóngyì ba?
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: To carry on the Four Modernizations we need a lot of educated people, but this can't be accomplished in a short time. You probably agree with that point, don't you?
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Wǒ dǒng, wǒ dǒng.
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: I understand, I understand.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Suǒyǐ, wǒmen bàn yìxiē zhòngdiǎn xuéxiào, wèide shi jiākuài jiàoyù sùdù.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: So we are setting up some key schools in order to speed up the educational process.

ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Jiākuài jiàoyù sùdù? Nǐde yìsi shi shuō, zhòngdiǎn xuéxiàode tiáojiàn bǐjiào hǎo, xuésheng, jiàoshīde shuǐpíng yě bǐjiào gāo, zhèiyang, xuésheng jiu yǒu jīhui zài bǐjiào duǎnde shíjiānli xué dào bǐjiào duōde dōngxi.

PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: To speed up the educational process? You mean, key schools have better conditions, and the level of their students and teachers is higher, so the students have the opportunity to learn more things in a shorter time.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Duì le.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Right.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Nàme nǐmen pài chū guóde liúxuéshēng shì bu shì dōu shi cóng zhòngdiǎn xuéxiàoli láide ne?
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Then are all the students you send abroad from key schools?
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Tāmen duōbànr shi cóng zhòngdiǎn dàxué láide, tèbié shi yánjiūshēng.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: They're mostly from key universities, especially the graduate students.

ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Wǒ jiànguo jǐwèi lái Měiguó niàn shūde liúxuéshēng, tāmen dōu shi xué kēxué jìshude. Tīngshuō tāmen xuéde fēicháng nǔlì. Zhōngguó liúxuéshēngde xuéxí zhòngdiǎn shi kēxué jìshu, duì bu duì?

PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: I've met several Chinese going to school in the United States. They were all studying science and technology. I hear that they were very hard-working. Chinese students abroad concentrate on science and technology, isn't that right?
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Nín shuōde duì, tāmen zhǔyào shi xué zìrán kēxué. Zhèi shi wǒmen mùqián zuì dàde xūyào.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: That's right, they mainly study the natural sciences. That's our greatest need at present.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Tāmen huí guó yǐhòu dōu gǎo yánjiū gōngzuò ma?
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: After they return home do they all do research work?

LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Bù yídìng. Wǒ xiǎng yǒu yí dà bùfen hái děi zài dàxué dānrèn jiàoshīde gōngzuò. Shíxiàn Sìge Xiàndàihuà líbukāi jiàoyù ma! Jiàoshòu, yǒu shíjiān gěi wǒ jièshao jièshao Měiguóde jiàoyù qíngkuàng a!

LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Not necessarily. I think that a large portion of them still have to take up teaching positions in universities. Education is essential to achieving the Four Modernizations! Professor, when you have the time, tell me about education in America!
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Hǎo, nǐ duì něifāngmiànde qíngkuàng zuì yǒu xìngqu?
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Sure. What aspect are you most interested in?
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Wǒ duì xiǎoxué jiàoyù, értóng jiàoyù zuì yǒu xìngqu, yīnwei, wǒ xiǎng yíge rén kāishǐ shòu jiàoyùde nèiduàn shíjiān shi fēicháng zhòngyàode.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: I'm most interested in primary school and child education, because I think the period when a person begins his education is very important.

ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Wǒ tóngyì nǐde kànfǎ, érqiě, chúle shàng xué yǐwài, jiātíng hé shèhuìde jiàoyù yě fēicháng zhòngyào. Yǒude shíhou, fùmǔmende jiàoyù qíngkuàng hé háizimen yǒu fēicháng dàde guānxi.

PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: I agree with you. Furthermore, besides attending school, the education one gets in the home and in society are also very important. Sometimes the parents' education has a great bearing on the children's.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Duì. Suǒyǐ gǎohǎo jiàoyù shi zhěnggèr shèhuìde gōngzuò, wǒmen měige rén dōu yǒu zérèn.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Right. So improving education is the job of our entire society. Each of us has the responsibility for it.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Nǐ shuōde zhēn hǎo. Duì le, jīntian wǒmen cānguānde Běidà, shì bu shì Zhōngguó zuì hǎode dàxué ne?
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Well said. Oh yes--is Běijīng University, which we're going to visit today, the best university in China?

LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Běidà shi hěn yǒu míngde dàxué, kěshi hěn nán shuō shì bu shì zuì hǎode. Zài Zhōngguó yǒu jǐge dàxué dōu bú cuò. Běidàde jiàoyù zhìliàng jīběnshang ràng rén mǎnyì. Shíjiān bù zǎo le, nín chī zǎofàn le meiyou?

LÍN XIǍOHÉ: B.U. is a very famous university, but it's difficult to say if it's the best. There are several universities in China that are pretty good. The quality of education at B.U. is basically satisfactory. It's getting late, have you had breakfast?
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Ōu, wǒ hái méi chī zǎofàn ne, wǒ mǎshàng jiù qù.
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Oh, I haven't had breakfast yet. I'll go right away.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: Bié jí, wǒmen děngzhe nín.
LÍN XIǍOHÉ: No hurry, we'll wait for you.
ĀMǓSĪZHUÀNG JIÀOSHÒU: Hǎo, wǒ hěn kuài jiù lái.
PROFESSOR ARMSTRONG: Okay, I'll be there shortly.
